subject: Transient asymmetric routing + policy rewrite causing SNAT port pressure — private cutover triage
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@blueleaf.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood-inference.com
Cc: netops@blueleaf.com
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent 502s and TCP stalls after private cutover

Connor —

We cut the private connectivity handoff at 03:00 PT this morning and immediately started seeing intermittent 502s on our ingest endpoints. Application logs show long TCP stalls (retransmits, zero-window) for a subset of clients behind our NAT. Short summary: ~2-3% of requests hit 502s, timing out after retries.

I attached a small pcap from one affected client span (blueleaf-cutover-20251210.pcap) — you can see retransmits and a lot of duplicated SYNs. We rolled back two firewall rules at 06:30 which improved but did not fully resolve.

Top of mind: cutover included a firewall policy rewrite (consolidated outbound L4 rules and a new DNAT/SNAT policy). Any obvious things for us to check?

Thanks,
Alice
Network Ops — Blueleaf Systems
[attachment: blueleaf-cutover-20251210.pcap (12.4MB)]

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@blueleaf.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s and TCP stalls after private cutover

Thanks Alice — remote capture is helpful. Looping in Marissa (CS lead for Blueleaf) and Karthik from infra to help triage.

Quick asks so we can prioritize:
- Can you share which firewall policy exactly was applied (policy-id or commit hash)?
- Did you change SNAT pools or the SNAT algorithm during the cutover?
- Any asymmetric routing observed in your monitoring (packets egress one path, return on another)?

Initial hypotheses:
- MSS/clamping mismatch across the new firewall path causing fragmentation/retransmits
- SNAT port exhaustion / port reuse amplifying retransmits when return path changes
- A short-lived ACL rewrite that dropped return TCP segments (asymmetric policy)

Immediate next steps we recommend:
1) Preserve a 5-minute pcap window (you already attached one — thanks).
2) Snapshot conntrack/ephemeral port usage on the affected NAT gateway at high resolution.
3) If possible, temporarily pin egress for one affected client to the old path to test for asymmetry.

Marissa/Karthik — assigning to you for analysis. I will coordinate with Blueleaf and if we need an on-call bridge.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@blueleaf.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood-inference.com
Cc: netops@blueleaf.com
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s and TCP stalls after private cutover

Connor —

Policy commit: fw-commit-20251210-382 (we pushed a rule consolidation + NAT rewrite). We did change the SNAT pool size: previously 12k ports per host, after cutover it was set to 8k (attempt to limit port churn during consolidation).

We saw asymmetric routes in perf dashboards for ~5% of flows (egress via private-edge-1, return via transit-link-b). We rolled back the new ACLs to previous state at 06:30 and that reduced 502s to ~0.5% but didn't eliminate them.

Attached another screenshot of the ACL diff (fw-acl-diff-20251210.png).

We'll keep captures coming. Happy to stand up a packet-level call if needed.

—Alice
[attachment: fw-acl-diff-20251210.png (320KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood-inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@blueleaf.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 11:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s and TCP stalls after private cutover — analysis notes

Folks — I dug into the pcap and asked Blueleaf for conntrack snapshots. Key findings:
- The pcap shows repeated SYN retransmits with no SYN-ACKs for a short window; later we see SYN-ACKs arriving on a different path (sequence numbers match). Classic asymmetric return.
- Blueleaf's conntrack dump at 09:05 shows SNAT ephemeral port utilization at ~96% for the affected gateway (approx 7.7k/8k ports in use).
- There's also evidence of MSS clamping mismatch: MSS advertised 1460 end-to-end but the new firewall path reduces MTU (due to an inline inspection hop adding 60 bytes), so fragments/retransmits are likely for large requests.

Proposed mitigation (ordered):
1) Immediately increase SNAT pool back to 12k (restore previous capacity) — low risk, high ROI.
2) Apply a temporary route pin for problematic public IPs so return path matches egress.
3) Add MSS clamp on the client-facing firewall to 1380 to avoid fragmentation until inspection path is updated.
4) After stabilization, schedule a controlled traffic-shift to validate the consolidated policy and monitor conntrack headroom.

I attached a short runbook (runbook-snatchange-v1.docx) with CLI commands we should run. If Blueleaf can increase SNAT pool now, that should remove the port starvation amplification and drop rate.

—Karthik
Infra — Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook-snatchange-v1.docx (24KB)]

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@blueleaf.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Transient asymmetric routing + policy rewrite causing SNAT port pressure — private cutover triage

Alice — thanks for the screenshots and quick responses. Per Karthik's guidance we coordinated with Blueleaf ops at 13:15 PT yesterday and they applied the following changes:
- Increased SNAT pool for the affected gateway from 8k -> 12k ports.
- Added temporary policy pin for the top-10 affected client IPs to force symmetric egress/return.
- Enabled MSS clamp to 1380 on the inspection hop.

Outcome after changes: 0.1% 502s during the 6 hour window; tcp retransmits in sampled pcaps dropped by ~95%. Blueleaf will keep the increased SNAT pool while they run a staged consolidation with a canary route.

Action items and follow-ups:
- Blueleaf: schedule a controlled test for policy consolidation with traffic mirroring and a canary group (recommended window: low-traffic hours).
- Redwood: we will provide a short checklist for future cutovers documenting conntrack headroom checks + MSS verification.

Closing the escalation for now; feel free to reopen if you see regressions. Thanks to Marissa and Karthik for the fast turnaround.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
